newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge dissidents recognise government.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge dissidents recognise government.

text.p: Breakaway Khmer Rouge guerrillas loyal to Ieng Sary recognise the authority of the Cambodian government and the ideals of a single state, territory and administration, co-Premier Hun Sen said on Saturday.

The second prime minister, speaking at the opening of a women's training centre, said the guerrillas who have broken away from hardliners led by Pol Pot had also recognised a 1994 law that banned the Maoist Khmer Rouge movement.

"They recognise the royal Cambodian government, including the law that outlawed the Khmer Rouge, and they want their army and people to live with the royal government under one state, one territory, one national administration," Hun Sen said.
"The Khmer Rouge is one step from the end," added the premier, who on Monday met senior leaders of the breakaway guerrilla faction for the first time.
In Thailand on Thursday, Co-Defence Ministers Tea Banh and Tea Chamrath held the highest level talks to date with Ieng Sary, who was foreign minister during the brutal 1975-79 Khmer Rouge rule.

The ministers said the talks had been fruitful, but Tea Chamrath said they did not know when a final agreement would be reached. One sticking point had been what to do with Ieng Sary, who was sentenced to death in absentia for his role in the 1970s genocide.
